title: Chemical Identity Reconciliation and Public Database Assessment of a Fisetin Aminoethyl Ether
content: AI-assisted nomination of phytochemical derivatives requires a verifiable molecular identity and a search that distinguishes exact structures from neighbouring analogues. This computational communication specifies AIIP-FIS-7O-DMAE-001, fisetin 7-O-[2-(dimethylamino)ethyl] ether, proposed in an author-held immunopharmacology book manuscript. The graph retains the flavonol double bond and free 3, 3′ and 4′ hydroxyl groups. The reported RDKit analysis gives C19H19NO6, molecular weight 357.36 g/mol, monoisotopic mass 357.1212373 Da and InChIKey SVQICVJPUYZYSA-UHFFFAOYSA-N, correcting the source formula and mass. Relative to fisetin, calculated polar surface area decreases from 111.13 to 103.37 Å² and neutral Crippen cLogP increases from 2.2824 to 2.5172. Searches completed on 12 October 2026 returned no matching candidate record in PubChem identity searches or ChEBI and ChEMBL InChIKey queries, with successful parent controls. PubChem returned 47 substructure records; their retrieved formulae and keys differed from the candidate. Additional aminoethyl-flavonoid literature and a registered fisetin aminoethyl conjugate establish substantial prior modification precedent. Incomplete literature drawing coverage and specialist patent analysis keep exact-structure novelty provisional. The project code identifies the computational structure and is not evidence of AI generation, synthesis, antibody binding or efficacy.
